# Rule register (US, EU, UK)

A dated list of consumer-protection rules that persuasion mechanics most often engage. It supports risk triage; it is not legal advice and it never concludes that an element is lawful.

How to use it:
- Default jurisdictions are US (federal, plus California where noted), EU and UK; use only the ones the user names if they name any. App-store rows only when the user says the flow runs inside that store's app.
- For each element: find its DP row, state the "legitimate only if" fact, list the facts the user must confirm, list the source rows it may engage per jurisdiction with their read dates, give the severity, then the honest version.
- Staleness: compare each source row's read date with today's date. If more than 6 months have passed, mark that row "stale: re-check" in the output. All rows below were read on 2026-10-03, so they turn stale after 2027-04-03.
- National rules: EU member states may add stricter rules (for example Germany's mandatory online cancel button for contracts concluded on a website, §312k BGB, https://www.gesetze-im-internet.de/bgb/__312k.html, read 2026-10-03). This register does not cover national rules; say so when the user sells into one country.
- Close every register table with: "Not legal advice. Rules last read on [dates]; re-check any rule read more than 6 months before today."

Pattern names follow published taxonomies: Mathur et al. 2019 (ledger L29); OECD, "Dark commercial patterns", Digital Economy Papers No. 336, 2022 (https://doi.org/10.1787/44f5e846-en); the FTC staff report (US-11); CMA, "Online choice architecture" discussion paper CMA155, April 2022 (https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/online-choice-architecture-how-digital-design-can-harm-competition-and-consumers). Read 2026-10-03.

## Severity (risk triage, not a verdict)

| Level | Meaning |
|---|---|
| High | If the facts are as described, the element likely engages a named prohibition below. Fix the fact or remove the element before it goes live. |
| Medium | A disclosure or design change is needed for the "legitimate only if" fact to hold. |
| Review | A judgment call: the outcome depends on details. Record the reasoning and the fact relied on; counsel if in doubt. |

When the user has not said whether the fact holds, give the severity for both cases ("High if the timer restarts; Review if the offer really ends then") and list the fact under "facts to confirm".

## Patterns

| Id | Pattern | Legitimate only if | Facts to confirm | US | EU | UK | Severity | Honest version |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| DP-01 | Countdown or deadline | The offer really ends at the time shown, for everyone, and the timer does not restart | Real end date; does it reset per visitor, session or day; what happens after it ends | US-1 | EU-1 (Annex I point 7) | UK-1 (Sch. 20 para 7) | High if it resets or the offer continues; Review if the end is real | State the real end date in words, or drop the timer; give a true reason to act now (price change date, cohort start) |
| DP-02 | Low stock or limited places | The number comes from live inventory or capacity and is current | Data source; refresh rate; what "left" counts | US-1 | EU-1 (Arts. 6-7) | UK-1 (Sch. 20 para 20) | High if invented or static; Review if live | Show the real count from the inventory system, or state the real capacity limit and why it exists |
| DP-03 | Activity and popularity messages ("23 people viewing", "most popular") | Real data, with the basis and period stated or available on request | Data source; period; how "popular" is defined | US-1 | EU-1 (Arts. 6-7; Annex I point 23c for social endorsements) | UK-1 | High if invented; Medium if real but the basis is not stated | "Chosen by 61% of teams that signed up in May" with a source, or remove |
| DP-04 | Reviews, testimonials, ratings, endorsements | From real customers about real experience; not bought for positive sentiment; negative ones not hidden; incentives and connections disclosed; reasonable steps to check origin | Collection method; incentives and whether they depended on a positive review; moderation policy; staff or relative reviews | US-2, US-3 | EU-1 (Annex I points 23b, 23c) | UK-1 (Sch. 20 para 13) | High if fake, bought, suppressed or an undisclosed insider review; Medium if checks on origin are missing (EU-1 point 23b) | Ask every customer at the same moment, publish all ratings, show how reviews are checked, label incentivised reviews, keep originals |
| DP-05 | "Was/now" price or percent off | EU: the "was" price is the lowest price of the 30 days before the cut, and the percentage is computed from it. US: the former price was genuinely offered in good faith for a reasonably substantial period. UK: the claim is not misleading | Price history for the prior 30 days or more; how long the old price applied; any sales at it | US-4, US-1 | EU-2, EU-3 | UK-1 (general rules), UK-5; UK-7 is a proposal | High if the history does not support it | Show the 30-day lowest price as the reference, or drop the comparison and state the current price |
| DP-06 | Drip or hidden fees | The total price including mandatory fees is shown up front | Which fees are mandatory; where they first appear | US-5 for tickets and short stays; US-1 otherwise | EU-1 (Art. 7), EU-4 (Art. 6) | UK-2 | High in the UK and for US tickets or lodging; Medium elsewhere | Show the all-in price first; list optional extras separately |
| DP-07 | Pre-ticked paid extras or items added to the basket | Every paid extra is opt-in | Default state of each box; how the item got into the basket | US-1 (US-6 if recurring) | EU-4 (Art. 22) | UK-4 | High | Unticked boxes with the price beside each, extras offered as a separate choice |
| DP-08 | Confirmshaming ("No thanks, I like paying more") | The decline option is worded neutrally | Exact wording of both options | US-1, US-11 | EU-1 (Arts. 8-9, fact-dependent) | UK-1 | Review; Medium when combined with other pressure | "No thanks" next to "Yes, send me the guide" |
| DP-09 | Cancelling harder than signing up | Cancelling takes no more steps or channels than joining; at most one save offer, skippable in one click | Steps and screens for each path (see the symmetry table); channel (online, chat, phone); customer location | US-6; US-8 for California; never US-7 | EU-1 (Art. 9(d)); EU-5 when a withdrawal right exists; EU-6 Art. 25(3) only for online platforms | UK-1 (general rules); UK-3 is not in force | High when online sign-up must be cancelled by phone or chat; Medium when extra screens cannot be skipped | Cancel in the same place and channel as sign-up, one optional offer with "Cancel anyway" equally prominent, confirmation by email |
| DP-10 | Free trial turning into a paid plan; pre-selected annual billing; a switch that changes the plan | Price, charge date, renewal terms and how to cancel are shown before billing details; express consent to the renewal; reminders where required; nothing is charged before the stated date | Screens before card entry; consent mechanism; reminder emails; default plan; order-button wording | US-6, US-8 | EU-1 (Arts. 6-7; Annex I point 20), EU-4 (Art. 6; Art. 8(2): price, duration and how to end shown directly before the order, button says ordering means paying, otherwise the consumer is not bound) | UK-1 (Sch. 20 para 23 and general rules); UK-3 not in force | High if terms appear only after card entry or the switch changes the plan silently; Medium if shown but not prominent | Show "Free for 7 days, then $X per year on [date]; cancel any time in Settings" next to the button, and send a reminder |
| DP-11 | Nagging: repeated prompts after a "no" | A "no" is remembered for a reasonable period | How often the prompt returns; whether it can be dismissed for good | US-1 | EU-1 (Art. 8; Annex I point 26 when the prompts come by email, phone or other remote media); EU-6 Art. 25(3) only for online platforms | UK-1 (Sch. 20 para 28 for persistent solicitations) | Review | "Not now" and "Don't ask again" options; respect them |
| DP-12 | Unequal choices: consent banners, plan pickers | Accept and reject (or the options offered) are equally easy and prominent; nothing optional is pre-ticked; withdrawing is as easy as consenting | Clicks to reject vs accept; default states | US-9 for California | EU-7, EU-8, EU-9 | UK-6 | Medium for consent banners; Review for plan pickers | Equal buttons on the first layer; a persistent link to change choices |
| DP-13 | Gamified expiring rewards, streak loss, guilt messages | Rewards follow real progress, not app opens; expiry is real and stated; no fear or loss threats | Expiry rules; message wording | US-1 | EU-1 (Arts. 8-9, fact-dependent) | UK-1 | Review; High if the expiry is false (see DP-01) or aimed at children (DP-14) | Reward completed progress; plain reminders without loss threats |
| DP-14 | Pressure aimed at children or other vulnerable groups | Not used | Audience age; targeting criteria | US-1, US-10 | EU-1 (Annex I point 28); EU-6 Art. 28 for platforms | UK-1 (Sch. 20 para 30) | High | Address parents or adults; no urgency or exhortation aimed at children |
| DP-15 | Paywall trial toggle inside an iOS app | Use only when the user says the flow is in an iOS app | Is it an iOS app; what the toggle changes | — | — | — | Review; AP-1 (vendor-reported review practice as of 2026-01, not guideline text). Web and Android flows use DP-10 and get no Apple row | Separate, clearly labelled plans with the trial terms stated on the plan that has the trial |
| DP-16 | Ads dressed up as editorial or independent content | Paid content is clearly marked | Who paid; how it is labelled | US-3, US-1 | EU-1 (Annex I point 11) | UK-1 (Sch. 20 para 12) | High | Label it "Advertisement" or "Paid partnership" at the top |

## Cancellation symmetry table (for DP-09 and DP-10)

| | Sign up | Cancel |
|---|---|---|
| Channel (web, app, chat, phone) | | |
| Steps (clicks, screens) | | |
| Fields to fill | | |
| Mandatory contact (call, chat) | | |
| Offers or questions shown before completion | | |
| Confirmation | | |

Count from the user's description; write "not stated" rather than guessing. Add the EU-5 line when the customer is in the EU, the contract was concluded online and a withdrawal right exists: "Is a 'withdraw from contract here' function available throughout the withdrawal period?"
